newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia c.bank sells HRK78 mln bills, rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Croatia c.bank sells HRK78 mln bills, rates steady.

text.p: The National Bank of Croatia sold 78 million kuna in its 35- and 91-day liquidity bills at an auction on Wednesday, less than half the amount the banking sector invested a week ago despite higher liquidity.
The issued rates were a steady 7.50 and 9.0 percent, respectively, now entering the third month.
Commercial banks still showed no interest in the longest maturity of 182 days, last sold at 17.50 percent last autumn.
The central bank said it would probably refrain from open market interventions this week after its cut in the reserve requirement released more kuna into the banking system.
Monday's reserve payment drained a total of 3.35 billion kuna, a net 47.6 million less than a fortnight ago.

The actual effect of the March cut in the reserve ratio by one percentage point to under 35 percent was weaker than the expected 100 million as the domestic currency deposits rose in the meantime, a central bank official told Reuters.
